claims.text: Conventional W-particle or connected-W-region/Cu-matrix composites tend to contain interfacial voids.
Conventional W–Cu composites tend to exhibit phase separation.
Electroless plating or a comparable technique can apply a thin, uniform Ni coating to W particles.
A Ni interlayer will enhance wetting between W and Cu during spark-plasma sintering.
Ni-coated W particles will form a graded W–Ni–Cu interfacial layer during spark-plasma sintering.
The Ni coating reduces W/Cu interfacial energy.
The Ni coating enables greater diffusion and interfacial bonding between W and Cu.
A graded W–Ni–Cu transition zone minimizes abrupt phase boundaries.
The graded interfacial zone reduces interfacial void formation.
Ni pre-coating reduces phase separation in W–Cu composites.
Interfacial voids and phase separation impair thermal transport in W–Cu composites.
A graded W–Ni–Cu interface contributes to solid-solution strengthening.
The graded interface improves mechanical integrity under irradiation.
Relative to vapor-coated W powders consolidated by spark-plasma sintering, Ni-coated samples will have a lower void fraction.
Relative to the named baseline, Ni-coated samples will have more uniform interfacial contact.
Relative to the named baseline, Ni-coated samples will have improved thermal conductivity.
Relative to the named baseline, Ni-coated samples will maintain or improve mechanical durability under simulated fusion-reactor conditions.
Vapor-coated W powders consolidated by spark-plasma sintering can exhibit near-perfect W/Cu contact.
The vapor-coated W-powder baseline still exhibits occasional voids and phase separation that affect thermal transport.
Spark-plasma sintering below 1000 °C in an inert atmosphere is the proposed consolidation boundary.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify spark-plasma sintering below 1000 °C, while the mechanism explicitly relies on wetting by molten copper during sintering. Copper is not molten under that stated temperature boundary.

The predicted comparison baseline is vapor-coated W powder processed by spark-plasma sintering, but the experimental control is described merely as uncoated W particles. The experiment therefore does not clearly test the claimed outcome against the named baseline.
